# 2. Di chuyển — đi + chạy nhanh, mỗi kiểu một ảnh 3 hướng (144 lính)

> Sinh tự động bởi `docs/art/prompts/gen_prompts.py` (dữ liệu lấy thẳng từ `packages/core`). Sửa ở script rồi chạy lại
> `python3 docs/art/prompts/gen_prompts.py`, đừng sửa tay file này.

- Ảnh lưu theo hệ ở `docs/art/topdown/<hệ>/` (tên ghi cạnh từng prompt), cạnh `rigs.json` của hệ đó.
- Mỗi kiểu chuyển động **một ảnh 3 hàng** (hàng 1 ngang quay **trái**, hàng 2 trước, hàng 3 sau): `<lính>-idle.png`,
  `<lính>-walk.png`, `<lính>-run.png`, `<lính>-attack.png`, `<lính>-skill.png`.
- Luôn **đính kèm bảng 4 mặt** (`<lính>-views.png`, tạo ở file 1) của chính lính đó để giữ đúng màu, tóc, đồ, cỡ pixel.
- `build_topdown_sprite.py` tự nhận ảnh 3 hàng `<lính>-<kiểu>.png` và các ảnh `<lính>-<kiểu>-side|front|back.png` có đủ 3
  hướng thành `anim.<kiểu>`. Nhìn ngang AI lỡ vẽ quay phải thì khai `"flip": ["left"]` cho kiểu đó trong `rigs.json`.
- Xem trước khi dùng: đủ khung, các khung không chạm nhau, cùng cỡ, chân cùng một vạch đất, **mọi khung cùng một hướng**,
  nền trong suốt thật (không phải ô caro vẽ giả). Sai thì tạo lại, đừng cố cứu.

Mỗi lính 2 prompt, mỗi prompt **một ảnh 3 hàng × 6 khung** (hàng 1 ngang quay trái, hàng 2 trước, hàng 3 sau), lặp lại,
đứng tại chỗ (không trượt ngang khung); dáng mang chất riêng của hệ:

1. **Đi** (di chuyển bình thường): luôn một chân chạm đất, nhún tối đa 1 px (thích khách rón rén cúi thấp, thú cưỡi
   nước kiệu, máy lăn chậm, tinh linh / bóng ma / tiên cá trôi nhấp nhô, thuỷ quái bò bằng xúc tu). Lưu `<lính>-walk.png`
   → `anim.walk`.
2. **Chạy nhanh** (giữ Shift): bám đất, **không nhảy** — người đổ về trước, sải chân dài, tay đánh mạnh, vải bay ra sau
   (thích khách lướt thấp, thú cưỡi phi nước đại, khiên binh xông sau khiên, khổng lồ lao rầm rập, máy bị đẩy rung bánh).
   Lưu `<lính>-run.png` → `anim.run`.

Hàng trước / sau đi kiểu nhân vật RPG 16-bit đi xuống / đi lên màn hình: chân nhấc lên hạ xuống, người luôn chính diện.

## 1. ☀️ Thánh Quang Điện — Temple of Light (hệ Quang)

Dáng đi của hệ: *upright, proud and steady steps, the cape swaying evenly*.

**1. Thợ mỏ** (×0.9)

*Đi 3 hướng* → đính kèm `docs/art/topdown/light/miner-views.png`, lưu thành `docs/art/topdown/light/miner-walk.png` (3 hàng × 6 khung: ngang / trước / sau)

```
Pixel art sprite sheet: ONE image, 3 rows x 6 columns (18 equal frames, evenly spaced, nothing touching another frame; frames about 61 x 43 px native per frame), a looping 6-frame WALK animation of the SAME character as in the attached model sheet. Row 1 = SIDE view facing LEFT, row 2 = FRONT view, row 3 = BACK view; frames go left to right in time order; within a row the feet stay on one ground line at the same spot (in place, no travelling).

ONE DIRECTION PER ROW (the most important rule)
- Row 1: SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT in EVERY frame: head, chest, hips and feet all point LEFT; only ONE eye visible at the left edge of the head; the face never turns toward the viewer; never two eyes, the face turning toward the viewer, facing right, a front or back view.
- Row 2: FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on in EVERY frame: both eyes visible, chest and hips square to the viewer, the body left-right symmetrical apart from the held gear, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing down the screen; never a profile, a single eye, the head or body turned sideways, a back view.
- Row 3: BACK view, the back to the viewer in EVERY frame: no eyes, no face and no profile visible, shoulders and hips square, the cloth covering the back, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing up the screen; never any eye or face, a profile, the head or body turned sideways, a front view.
- Every frame of a row is a redraw of that row's model view; between frames only the legs, the arms, the cloth and the bob change. Nobody turns, nothing switches to another view, no 3/4 angle.
- Final check before finishing, count the eyes in every frame, the LAST frame of each row included: row 1 = ONE eye in all 6 frames, row 2 = TWO eyes (the face) in all 6 frames, row 3 = NO eyes (the back) in all 6 frames. Fix any frame that breaks this; never let a row end in another view.

CHARACTER (Temple of Light civilization, Light element, gold miner "Miner"), identical in all 18 frames: same colours, gear, size and pixel scale
- Build: chibi stickman with a big round head (about a third of the total height) and a short body, slightly smaller and leaner, about 90% of a normal stickman. Size: about 18 x 18 px footprint, about 32 px tall.
- Head: big spiky glowing golden hair with a bright white four-pointed star in it, bold pixel clusters hugging the head. Black face, no mouth, no nose; slanted glowing golden eyes (2-pixel clusters with a white core pixel): TWO eyes in the front view, only ONE eye at the front edge of the head in the side view, no eyes in the back and top views.
- Body: solid black body with thin glowing golden crack lines on the limbs, a small brown cloth gold sack with a golden drawstring on a strap at the hip, gold nuggets peeking out.
- Cloth: short scarf in rich gold (#e8a91c), ragged stepped pixel edges, hanging close to the body.
- Gear: glowing pickaxe; every glowing part in radiant gold (#ffd84a).
- Pose: the pickaxe resting on the shoulder, a small gold sack bouncing at the hip.

GEAR LOCK (check every one of the 18 frames)
- Always drawn, complete, same size and same colours in EVERY frame: glowing pickaxe; a small brown cloth gold sack with a golden drawstring on a strap at the hip.
- The weapon / tool stays in the same hand; when the body hides part of it, the visible ends still show. A frame without the weapon or tool is wrong.

WALK (frame 6 loops back to frame 1)
- Row 1 (SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT, redrawn from cell 2 (SIDE view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) contact: the front foot lands heel first, the back leg straight behind, arms swinging opposite.
2. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) down: the body dips 1 px as the weight lands on the front leg, knee bent.
3. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) passing: the back leg swings forward past the standing leg, body back to neutral height.
4. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) up: the standing leg pushes off, the body rises 1 px, the swinging foot reaches forward.
5. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) contact (other side): the other foot lands heel first, legs swapped compared with frame 1.
6. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) passing (other side): the back leg swings forward again, the loop returning to frame 1.
- Row 2 (FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on, redrawn from cell 3 (FRONT view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) the left foot steps 1 px lower than the right, the right foot lifted 2 px with the knee bent; arms swing up and down at the sides.
2. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) both feet side by side again, body dips 1 px.
3. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) neutral height, feet side by side.
4. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) mirror of frame 1: the right foot 1 px lower, the left foot lifted 2 px.
5. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) both feet side by side, body dips 1 px.
6. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) neutral height, the same view as frame 1 of this row, ready to loop.
- Row 3 (BACK view, the back to the viewer, redrawn from cell 4 (BACK view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) the left foot steps 1 px lower than the right, the right foot lifted 2 px with the knee bent; arms swing up and down at the sides.
2. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) both feet side by side again, body dips 1 px.
3. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) neutral height, feet side by side.
4. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) mirror of frame 1: the right foot 1 px lower, the left foot lifted 2 px.
5. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) both feet side by side, body dips 1 px.
6. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) neutral height, the same view as frame 1 of this row, ready to loop.
- Row 1 is a classic side-scroller walk cycle seen purely in profile: the head stays in profile the whole time.
- Rows 2-3 read flat, like a 16-bit RPG sprite walking down / up the screen, no turning: the legs alternate stepping in place, the body bobbing 1 px, arms swinging.
- Gait of this civilization: upright, proud and steady steps, the cape swaying evenly; a few tiny golden star pixels touching the heels in the contact frames.
- A calm normal walk (the default way the unit moves): one foot always on the ground, the body bobs at most 1 px.
- Hair and cloth trail behind the motion.

STYLE
- Chunky pixel art: every art pixel a crisp square block, upscaled with nearest neighbour.
- 3-tone shading (cool dark shadow, saturated mid-tone, warm highlight), bold 1px dark outline.
- Arms, legs, weapon shafts and staffs at least 2 px thick.
- Glows are solid bright pixel clusters with a white-hot core; every effect is a solid pixel shape touching the body, the weapon or the ground line, nothing floating.
- Strictly orthographic: no perspective, no 3/4 angle.
- Background: fully transparent PNG (alpha). No white, no colour, no checkerboard pattern.

AVOID: text, labels, numbers, grid lines, borders, ground shadow, motion blur, speed lines, glow halo, bloom, gradients, anti-aliasing, 1-pixel thin lines, floating particles, extra limbs, a second weapon, cells of different sizes, the character changing size, a 3/4 head or body turn, the body turning to show a step, a swing or the cloth, realistic or painterly style, 3D render, any row with frames in another view, a missing or half-drawn weapon or tool, dust clouds, jumping, hopping, both feet in the air.
```

Pixel art sprite sheet: ONE image, 3 rows x 6 columns (18 equal frames, evenly spaced, nothing touching another frame; frames about 71 x 50 px native per frame), a looping 6-frame fast SPRINT / RUN animation of the SAME character as in the attached model sheet. Row 1 = SIDE view facing LEFT, row 2 = FRONT view, row 3 = BACK view; frames go left to right in time order; within a row the feet stay on one ground line at the same spot (in place, no travelling).

ONE DIRECTION PER ROW (the most important rule)
- Row 1: SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT in EVERY frame: head, chest, hips and feet all point LEFT; only ONE eye visible at the left edge of the head; the face never turns toward the viewer; never two eyes, the face turning toward the viewer, facing right, a front or back view.

- Row 3: BACK view, the back to the viewer in EVERY frame: no eyes, no face and no profile visible, shoulders and hips square, the cloth covering the back, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing up the screen; never any eye or face, a profile, the head or body turned sideways, a front view.
